$comment: THE LEDGER. One row per command surface of this bin — 20 registry tools plus 11
CLI-only commands. It is not a hand-written list: apps/browser-tab-mcp/tests/
surface-coverage.contract.test.ts enumerates the surfaces from makeAppRegistry()
and from commander (tests/helpers/cli-surface.ts) and fails if this file has a gap
or an orphan. Adding tool #21 turns that test red on the next `pnpm test`.
`tier` is where a surface's EFFECT is proved — that a browser actually did the
thing — not where it is dispatch-tested. A fake adapter and installFakeChrome
both stand in for a browser; neither is one, so neither counts here.
`evidence` is a path or the literal "pending". "pending" claims nothing and is
always honest. A non-pending chromium-e2e entry is a CLAIM, and e2e/run-guard.ts
enforces it: the run fails unless a PASSING test carried the matching
`surface` annotation. That is the anti-vacuity rule — this repo has shipped five
harnesses that passed while proving nothing, and the ledger is not allowed to
A surface may appear in more than one tier when it has more than one PATHWAY.
focus_tab through the extension and focus_tab through AppleScript are different
code with different bugs; the Chromium suite cannot reach the second by
construction, so it gets its own macos-local row rather than being called done.

tiers.chromium-e2e: Playwright, apps/chrome-extension/e2e/ — the built dist/ in a real Chromium/Edge against a throwaway daemon. Runs in CI on all three legs.
tiers.cli-process: vitest, apps/browser-tab-mcp/tests/ — the built dist/cli.js spawned as a real process against a fake-adapter daemon. No browser. Runs in CI.
tiers.macos-local: pnpm sweep:macos, a developer's Mac only. Real osascript / screencapture / Safari History.db. CANNOT run in CI: GitHub's macOS runners have no logged-in GUI session, so `tell application` cannot work.

coverage.covers: answers while a real browser session is live — the canary's contract is that it is unaffected by anything the browser is doing

extension pathway: real tabs as x-handles with dataSource=extension and running=true from a live socket; the summary projection's tabCount matches chrome.tabs.query and --url narrows to matching tabs only
AppleScript pathway: t:<browser>:<numeric> handles with dataSource != extension — the handle-grammar difference only this tier can prove

extension pathway: activates the tab and raises its window; un-minimizes a REALLY minimized window (wasMinimized/windowState/windowFocused, cross-checked against chrome.windows.get); --no-raise leaves window focus exactly where it was
AppleScript pathway: clearing minimized BEFORE `set index to 1`. focus.test.ts mocks the runOsa return string, so it proves the decoder and never the script

extension pathway: cross-window move via chrome.tabs.move preserves scroll (roundtrip.e2e.test.ts, the crown jewel); plus --new-window landing in a window that did not previously exist, --index placing exactly, the append form reporting the tab's ACTUAL final index rather than tabs.move's echo, and a negative index refused at the boundary (move-tab.e2e.test.ts). The signed/same-window forms (to/by) resolve daemon-side into this same absolute wire form before the effect boundary — the translation is pinned at unit tier (move-resolve.test.ts, daemon/index.test.ts), not re-proved here
AppleScript pathways: Chromium close+reopen and Safari --allow-reload — asserting the tab lands AND that the page reloaded, since proving the documented state loss matters as much as proving the move
extension pathway: the tab exists in chrome.tabs.query with the returned x-handle, in the window asked for, and --no-activate does not steal the window's active tab
AppleScript pathway (`make new tab`)
extension pathway: the tab is GONE from chrome.tabs.query, not merely absent from a snapshot the daemon rebuilt after being told it worked
AppleScript pathway (baseline `close tab`, not in applescriptCaps because it is unconditional)

extension pathway: mute/unmute (real mutedInfo + the snapshot enrichment), pin/unpin (including Chrome relocating a pinned tab to index 0), navigate in place, reload really re-fetching (a DOM mutation is thrown away), duplicate producing a second real tab, and refusals for a missing --url and an unknown action. back/forward are in tab-history.e2e.test.ts (a REAL click gesture, both directions, plus Chrome's own "Cannot find a next page in history" rejection travelling the full error path); discard is isolated in tab-discard.e2e.test.ts, which asserts only that a real browser accepted it and REISSUED the tab id — a post-discard read is unreachable by construction
AppleScript pathway: navigate/reload everywhere, back/forward on Chromium only (Safari's dictionary has no verb)

create/add/update/remove(by tabIds AND dissolve-by-groupId)/move against real chrome.tabGroups — and THE DOGFOOD BUG: grouping window-1 tabs while window 2 is frontmost must not relocate them. Sabotage-verified against real Chrome (reverting the createProperties.windowId pin reproduces the relocation), where it was previously proven only against a fake stub's model of the surprise. Also the per-id stale handling: one dead id is skipped and REPORTED in payload.skippedTabIds, all-stale errors. Extension-only by design, so this tier is the ceiling for this surface, not a stepping stone
extension pathway: a real window appears in chrome.windows.getAll holding exactly the urls asked for, and --no-focus does not steal focus from the previously frontmost window
AppleScript pathway (`make new window`), including --display targeting through rust-accel list_displays()

extension pathway: minimized/normal transitions read back through chrome.windows.get, and --bounds applied VERBATIM (probed, not assumed — measured 2026-08-24 under --headless=new; real clamping behaviour stays macos-local)
AppleScript pathway: real geometry with tolerance (macOS clamps to the visible frame), plus minimized/normal transitions

extension pathway: the window is gone from chrome.windows.getAll AND its tabs are gone from chrome.tabs.query — a window that closed while orphaning its tabs is invisible to any assertion that only counts windows
AppleScript pathway (`close window`)

the REAL two-step scripting.executeScript against a real page over http (chrome.scripting is blocked on data: entirely, so this could not be done with the roundtrip spec's data: page): metadata reads the live <title>, text returns reader-extracted prose and strips page chrome, state observes a scroll position that exists nowhere in the HTML, the navEpoch cache serves a repeat read and --force bypasses it, and an AppleScript-generation handle is refused with a reason

write-then-read keyed by the URL the EXTENSION reported (post-redaction, post-normalisation) rather than one the test invented — a key mismatch would make notes silently unreadable; plus a miss on an un-annotated URL returning nothing rather than inventing or erroring

tier-1 tab capture: real captureVisibleTab bytes verified by the JPEG SOI marker and a size floor (so "a file exists" cannot pass for an empty one), the active-tab preflight REFUSING a background tab (a screenshot of the wrong tab is far worse than an error) with --focus fixing it, and the neither-id schema rejection. Flagged as the sweep's likeliest failure; measured working under --headless=new 2026-08-24
tier-2 window capture: real `screencapture -l <cgWindowId>` behind BROWSER_TAB_WINDOW_CAPTURE=1 + Screen Recording TCC. Today's unit tests shim the binary
coverage.notRun: correlation never produced a cgWindowId for this window — capture has nothing to target

coverage.covers: the full plan→apply loop against a REAL browser: a planned reverse applied through the daemon flips chrome.tabs.query's own order exactly, status success with empty residual, and a re-apply of the consumed plan is refused as stale (its own application moved the state it was planned against). PLUS the act pathway (Phase 5): applying a planned mute makes chrome.tabs.query mutedInfo true for every member (asserted false beforehand, so the check cannot pass on the fixture); a planned group puts every member in ONE real groupId, proving the batch-verb contract against the browser rather than our echo; and a destructive-classed act plan is refused by the same live-layout gate that refuses a cut

additive reconstruction against a REAL browser: predicate-selected sources copied cross-window, chrome.tabs.query confirms every SOURCE still alive, the copies carry the source URLs under NEW tab identities, and the bystander window arrangement is otherwise untouched

the destructive §9.4 sequence against a REAL browser: predicate-selected sources transferred cross-window, chrome.tabs.query confirms the sources GONE, a same-window bystander alive, and the replacements carrying the source URLs; the source-stays-open-on-failure half is pinned at unit tier over the recorded command stream (a per-item creation failure cannot be forced deterministically in a real run)

read-only planning against a REAL browser's window: the returned effects imply exactly the arrangement chrome.tabs.query shows would result, riskClass is live-layout, the browser state is asserted UNCHANGED after planning (a planner that mutates is the defect this row guards), and the planId round-trips. Also the §11 endState pathway: a declared two-window layout plans as live-layout with copy/cut counts zero, and the SAME spec's apply then makes chrome.tabs.query truth match the declaration in both windows. PLUS the act pathway (Phase 5): a verb fanned over a selection plans as live-layout for mute, and a state-losing verb (discard) plans as riskClass destructive — the verb-aware risk table asserted against a REAL browser rather than a fixture

selector resolution against a REAL browser's tabs: a host-predicate selection and a signed-position selection each verified against BOTH the daemon result and chrome.tabs.query truth (the dual-truth rule), plus resolution metadata (snapshotToken present, live-move-domain uniformity true for a same-window selection)

real events, not a synthetic stream: a REAL committed navigation reaching `journey` with the browser's own transitionType and a navEpoch, the focus views asserted to be focus-only by design (recent/windowMru/tabMru return nav:[] unconditionally), and windowMru ordered by real onFocusChanged. Re-focus-driven MRU is NOT observable here — measured 2026-08-24, windows.update({focused:true}) on an existing window emits nothing under --headless=new — so that half is macos-local

AppleScript-mode browsers get COARSE events derived from StateStore diffs rather than extension frames — a different ingest path with different records. Also the half of windowMru the Chromium tier cannot reach: re-focusing an EXISTING window, which emits nothing under --headless=new because there is no window manager

Chrome-family: a real chrome.history.search finding a URL this run actually visited, and the `sources` array present on every result naming each source considered (the contract that exists because Chrome-only rows were otherwise indistinguishable from "Safari had nothing")
Safari: real sqlite3 against a fixture History.db by default; --real-history (Full Disk Access) is the only thing that proves FDA is granted

real chrome.bookmarks: create returns the new node's real id and the node is verifiable through chrome.bookmarks.get, search finds it, update renames it in the real tree, remove really deletes it (not just answers ok), and a javascript: URL is refused — a security boundary worth proving against the real command path rather than a mocked client

the TOOL HANDLER itself (invoked by nothing today — no integration test, no stress case; only the IPC method beneath it) answering with a real session behind it: pid, bound wsPort, the browser in `extensions`, a non-stale extensionInfo record, dataSource=extension and a non-zero real tab count. Plus the daemon-identity assertion re-stated as a named test so a regression names itself
the control, and the only CLI-level coverage this surface has: the input travels the real dispatcher and comes back, carrying the rust-vs-ts engine marker

both halves: hidden without MCP_DEV, and — the half nothing tested — `--source file` returning this run's own structured NDJSON records. Also pins that `--source memory` (the DEFAULT) is structurally EMPTY from a one-shot CLI, so changing that default turns the test red rather than passing silently. See BACKLOG B13

spawns the built bin's `mcp` subcommand and speaks real stdio JSON-RPC (initialize + tools/list), asserting a non-empty catalog that matches the registry's non-devOnly tools. FIRST coverage of runMcpServer THROUGH the subcommand — the stress harness spawns src/index.ts directly, so the commander wiring was driven by nothing. Sabotage-verified: renaming the command reddens it
piped (non-TTY) stdio takes the refusal branch: exit 1 and a reason naming the TTY. The App component's own tests never reach the CLI action

the action and checkLocalAccess() really run (no test invoked either before): a report with per-check lines, and the exit code asserted to AGREE with the headline verdict rather than to equal a fixed number — which keeps it honest on a machine where a check legitimately fails
the real Automation TCC probe and the non-prompting Screen Recording preflight. It reports what it finds; it cannot construct a DENIED state without revoking permission

the command reaches a REAL extension and its service worker really does not survive (sabotage-verified: an extension that acks without reloading fails it), plus the refusal for a browser with no connected extension. Neither "it disconnected" nor "it reconnected" is asserted — measured 2026-08-24, those go OPPOSITE ways by environment: headless never restarts the worker, real Windows Edge restarts it too fast to observe the drop. Writing this found B14 — the IPC client's 15s request timeout is shorter than the daemon's own 25s reload wait
the no-daemon error path (the half that needs no browser); the success path is chromium-e2e

the built bin's `operations` against a real spawned daemon: an empty journal answers [] over a real IPC round-trip, --id on an unknown record exits 1 with the ring-vs-archive hint, and a down daemon names itself as the missing dependency. Record-MINTING (copy_tabs writing a created-ids undo record that listOperations/getOperation then serve) is proven at the integration tier in tests/daemon-ipc.test.ts — the CLI client refuses copy/cut under BROWSER_TAB_FAKE_ADAPTER by design, so the built bin cannot mint here
spawned for real: polls to reachable, asserts status.pid is THIS process (not a stray daemon), then SIGTERM and asserts a clean exit 0. Executed by two harnesses today, asserted by neither

driven with BROWSER_TAB_PLATFORM forced to a platform with no service integration, so no LaunchAgent is ever registered on the machine running the suite: asserts a non-zero exit carrying the platform name and the actionable alternative. That proves the subcommand routes to serviceManager() and surfaces its answer — the untested wiring. The real install path is macos-local and opt-in
the real launchctl bootstrap. Opt-in and destructive to a developer's service state — expected to be CUT rather than automated
coverage.notRun: deliberate non-run: registering a LaunchAgent rewrites your own service state

coverage.covers: same forced-platform refusal routing; also pinned that `stop` and `uninstall` produce BYTE-IDENTICAL output, because they share a body DELIBERATELY (under KeepAlive a plain kill is undone) and the duplication must not be tidied away
prints a real token and a second call does NOT rotate it — the extension is holding that value

same forced-platform refusal routing, plus the byte-identical-to-uninstall assertion. Had zero behavioural coverage before: even the harnesses stop their daemons with SIGTERM rather than through this command
same forced-platform refusal routing. Had zero behavioural coverage before

piped stdin takes cli-kit's terminal:false branch: `noop hello` really runs through the dispatcher and echoes back, and `help` lists the REPL's own shortcuts. Driven under BOTH spellings — commander reports the `console` alias as a name, so a parity test sees it as present, but registered is not reachable
